title: Nine Columns of Ink
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：budget　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 budget 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 my mother was sent to balance ① a budget she could not read, and she said the reading was the whole of the lesson. The ② budget, meaning the sum and not the spending, was nine columns wide and was checked by whoever came last; a budget, she said, is the only thing in a ledger that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ budget in that ledger had the same date, and the ④ budget at the end, meaning the one the clerk kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever balanced properly. A budget, my grandmother said, is nine parts arithmetic and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the arithmetic is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ budget was the whole of the year, meaning the year it measured and not the sum. The ⑥ budget, meaning the year and not any of that, is the only thing in an office that everybody quotes and nobody questions; a budget, he said, is either something you balance or the only word that means both a sum and a year. She said the year is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ budget had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the arithmetic. The ⑧ budget of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine columns of ink and eleven years of balancing; a budget, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ budget I remember is the one at the end, which was signed in 1979 and is still described as the best in the county. A ⑩ budget, my grandmother said in 1982, is the only thing that improves by being kept; every budget, she said, is a year that has agreed to look like a sum. She said the year was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 预算（指那笔数目本身，与开销相对）
C. 固定搭配：balance a budget 平衡一笔预算
D. n. 预算（指账簿上每一份）
E. n. 预算（指末尾那一份）
F. n. 预算（抽象：它所衡量的那一年）
G. n. 那一年（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a budget she could not read
The budget, meaning the sum and not the spending
budget was the whole of the year
the budget had become a number in a report
The budget of the whole thing
A budget, my grandmother said in 1982

answers.why: balance a budget 意为“平衡一笔预算”，1959 年母亲被派去平衡一份她看不懂的预算。
budget 意为“预算”，指那笔数目本身而不是开销，共九栏，由最后走的人核对。
budget 指账簿上每一份预算，每一份都是同一个日期。
budget 指末尾那一份（办事员留的那一份），是唯一有人认真平衡过的。
budget 意为“预算”，抽象指它所衡量的那一年，父亲说 budget 就是那一年的全部。
budget 为抽象用法，指那一年本身，是办公室里人人都引用、却没人质疑的东西。
budget 意为“预算”，到 1974 年这份 budget 成了报告里的一个数字。
budget 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九栏墨水和十一年的平衡。
budget 意为“预算”，我记得的是末尾那一份，1979 年签字，至今仍被说成全县最好的。
budget 为抽象总称，祖母说预算是唯一会因为被守住而变好的东西。
